job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

response.passage: Many people believe that eating only one type of 'superfood' is enough to stay healthy, but this is a dangerous myth. A truly balanced diet requires a variety of food groups to provide all necessary nutrients. For instance, some think that roughage or fibre is useless because our bodies cannot digest it, but fibre is actually essential for smooth digestion and bowel health. Another common mistake is thinking that only oily snacks cause weight gain, while extra portions of rice or roti are harmless. In reality, the body converts any excess energy from carbohydrates into stored fat. Furthermore, many people mistakenly believe that white polished rice or maida are superior because they look cleaner and finer than whole grains. In truth, whole grains like millets and brown rice are far more nutritious as they retain the bran and germ. Finally, some assume that vegetarians cannot get enough protein without meat or eggs. This is incorrect, as pulses, legumes, and dairy are excellent plant-based protein sources that can easily meet our daily requirements. A balanced plate must include a mix of these diverse foods, tailored to your specific age and activity level, rather than following a one-size-fits-all approach.
response.summary: A healthy diet requires a variety of food groups rather than relying on a single food type. Whole grains, fibre, and diverse protein sources are essential for maintaining energy balance and overall health.
